solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.role: King who builds the temple and later turns away
solomon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solomon.importance: David has him anointed king at Gihon. He asks God for an understanding heart and builds the temple. Later his wives turn his heart to other gods. The LORD says he will tear the kingdom from Solomon’s son.
solomon.connections: Son of David and Bathsheba. Father of Rehoboam.

adonijah.name: Adonijah
adonijah.role: Royal son who claims the throne
adonijah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
adonijah.importance: He says, “I will be king,” and holds a feast with Joab and Abiathar. The feast ends when Solomon is anointed. Later he asks for Abishag as his wife. Solomon has Benaiah kill him.
adonijah.connections: Son of David and Haggith. Half-brother of Solomon.

abishag.name: Abishag
abishag.role: Young Shunammite who serves the aging David
abishag.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abishag.importance: She is brought to keep the old king warm, and she serves him. After David dies, Adonijah asks Bathsheba to get her as his wife. Solomon hears the request as a claim on the kingdom and has Adonijah killed.
abishag.connections: She serves King David. Adonijah later asks to marry her.

judgment-women.name: The two women before Solomon
judgment-women.role: Two unnamed women who both claim one baby
judgment-women.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
judgment-women.importance: One woman’s baby dies in the night. Each tells Solomon the living child is hers. Solomon calls for a sword to cut the child in two. One woman begs him to let the child live, and Solomon names her the mother.
judgment-women.connections: Both live in one house, and each has a baby. The text calls them prostitutes.

pharaoh-daughter-solomon.name: Pharaoh’s daughter, Solomon’s wife
pharaoh-daughter-solomon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
pharaoh-daughter-solomon.importance: Solomon marries her to join with Pharaoh king of Egypt. She lives in David’s city until Solomon builds her a house. Pharaoh gives her the city of Gezer as a wedding gift.
pharaoh-daughter-solomon.connections: Daughter of Pharaoh and wife of Solomon. She is not the princess who finds Moses.

adoniram.name: Adoniram
adoniram.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
adoniram.importance: He is over the men Solomon forces to work. Solomon sends thirty thousand of them to Lebanon in turns. He may be the Adoram of chapter 12, but that is a proposal.

hiram-artisan.name: Hiram, the bronze worker
hiram-artisan.role: Bronze worker who makes the temple pieces
hiram-artisan.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hiram-artisan.importance: Solomon brings him from Tyre. He casts the two bronze pillars, the sea, and the ten bases. He also makes the pots, shovels, and basins for the LORD’s house.
hiram-artisan.connections: His mother is a widow of Naphtali. His father is a bronze worker of Tyre. He is not King Hiram.

queen-sheba.name: The queen of Sheba
queen-sheba.role: Unnamed queen who tests Solomon with questions
queen-sheba.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
queen-sheba.importance: She hears of Solomon’s fame and comes to test him with hard questions. He answers them all. She praises his wisdom and blesses the LORD. She gives him gold, spices, and precious stones, then goes home.
queen-sheba.connections: She visits Solomon from her own land with her servants.

hadad-edom.name: Hadad
hadad-edom.role: Edomite royal child who flees to Egypt
hadad-edom.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hadad-edom.importance: Joab kills the males of Edom, and the child Hadad flees to Egypt. Pharaoh gives him a house, land, and a wife. When David and Joab die, he asks Pharaoh to let him go home. The LORD raises him as an enemy of Solomon.
hadad-edom.connections: One of the king’s offspring in Edom. Husband of Tahpenes’s sister and father of Genubath.

rezon.name: Rezon
rezon.role: Enemy of Solomon who rules in Damascus
rezon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
rezon.importance: He gathers men and leads a troop. They settle in Damascus, and he rules Syria. He is an enemy to Israel all the days of Solomon.
rezon.connections: Son of Eliada. He flees from his lord, Hadadezer king of Zobah.

jeroboam.name: Jeroboam
jeroboam.role: First king of the northern tribes
jeroboam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jeroboam.importance: Solomon puts him over the labor of the house of Joseph. Ahijah tears a garment and promises him ten tribes. He flees to Egypt, returns, and becomes king of Israel. He then makes two gold calves so the people will not go to Jerusalem.
jeroboam.connections: Son of Nebat and the widow Zeruah. Father of Abijah and Nadab.

ahijah-shiloh.name: Ahijah, the Shilonite
ahijah-shiloh.role: Prophet who promises Jeroboam ten tribes
ahijah-shiloh.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahijah-shiloh.importance: He tears a new garment into twelve pieces and gives Jeroboam ten. The ten pieces stand for ten tribes. Later he is old and cannot see. He still knows Jeroboam’s disguised wife and says her child will die.
ahijah-shiloh.connections: From Shiloh. He is not the scribe Ahijah or Baasha’s father Ahijah.

rehoboam.name: Rehoboam
rehoboam.role: King whose harsh answer divides Israel
rehoboam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
rehoboam.importance: The people ask him at Shechem to make their work lighter. He drops the old men’s advice and promises a heavier yoke. Israel turns from him, and he keeps Judah. In his fifth year Shishak takes the temple treasures.
rehoboam.connections: Son of Solomon and Naamah. Father of Abijam.

shishak.name: Shishak
shishak.role: King of Egypt who attacks Jerusalem
shishak.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shishak.importance: Jeroboam stays in Egypt with him until Solomon dies. In Rehoboam’s fifth year he comes against Jerusalem. He takes the treasures of the LORD’s house and the king’s house. He also takes Solomon’s gold shields.
shishak.connections: Jeroboam flees to him. He later attacks Rehoboam’s city.

tahpenes.name: Tahpenes
tahpenes.role: Queen of Egypt in Hadad’s story
tahpenes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
tahpenes.importance: Pharaoh gives her sister to Hadad as wife. Tahpenes weans their son Genubath in Pharaoh’s house. The text says nothing more about her.
tahpenes.connections: Wife of Pharaoh. Her sister marries Hadad.

genubath.name: Genubath
genubath.role: Son of Hadad raised in Egypt
genubath.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
genubath.importance: Tahpenes weans him in Pharaoh’s house. He lives there among Pharaoh’s sons. The text names him in one verse and tells no more.
genubath.connections: Son of Hadad. His mother is the sister of Tahpenes.

shemaiah.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah.role: Man of God who stops Rehoboam’s war
shemaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shemaiah.importance: Rehoboam gathers 180,000 warriors to win Israel back. Shemaiah gives God’s word: do not fight your brothers. The men listen and go home.
shemaiah.connections: He speaks to Rehoboam, Judah, and Benjamin.

adoram.name: Adoram
adoram.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
adoram.importance: He is over the men forced to work. Rehoboam sends him after Israel turns away. All Israel stones him to death, and Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem in his chariot.
adoram.connections: He serves Rehoboam. He may be the Adoniram of chapters 4 and 5, but that is a proposal.

judah-man-god.name: The man of God from Judah
judah-man-god.role: Unnamed man of God who speaks against Bethel’s altar
judah-man-god.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
judah-man-god.importance: He cries out against Jeroboam’s altar, and the altar splits. Jeroboam’s hand dries up, and the man prays until it is healed. He was told not to eat or drink there. An old prophet lies to him, and he eats. A lion kills him on the road.
judah-man-god.connections: He comes from Judah. He faces Jeroboam and then meets the old prophet of Bethel.

bethel-old-prophet.name: The older prophet at Bethel
bethel-old-prophet.role: Unnamed old prophet who lies to the man of God
bethel-old-prophet.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
bethel-old-prophet.importance: He rides after the man of God. He lies that an angel said to bring him home. At the table he speaks the LORD’s word against his guest. Later he buries the man in his own grave.
bethel-old-prophet.connections: He lives in Bethel. His sons tell him what the man of God did.

jeroboam-wife.name: Jeroboam’s wife
jeroboam-wife.role: Unnamed mother who visits Ahijah in disguise
jeroboam-wife.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jeroboam-wife.importance: Jeroboam sends her to Shiloh in disguise with bread, cakes, and honey. Ahijah cannot see, yet he knows her at the door. He gives her heavy news for Jeroboam’s house. She reaches Tirzah, and the child dies as she steps in.
jeroboam-wife.connections: Wife of Jeroboam. Mother of the sick child Abijah.

abijah-child.name: Abijah, Jeroboam’s son
abijah-child.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abijah-child.importance: He falls sick, and his mother goes to ask Ahijah about him. He dies when she comes home. All Israel buries him and mourns. He is not Abijam, the king of Judah.
abijah-child.connections: Son of Jeroboam and his unnamed wife.

naamah.name: Naamah
naamah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
naamah.importance: The text names her twice as Rehoboam’s mother. It tells nothing that she does.
naamah.connections: Mother of Rehoboam. The text calls her the Ammonitess.

abijam.name: Abijam
abijam.role: King of Judah between Rehoboam and Asa
abijam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abijam.importance: He rules three years in Jerusalem. He walks in his father’s sins and is at war with Jeroboam. The LORD still gives him a son to rule after him, for David’s sake.
abijam.connections: Son of Rehoboam. Maacah is called his mother.

asa.name: Asa
asa.role: King of Judah who removes idols and pays Syria
asa.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
asa.importance: He removes the idols and removes Maacah from being queen. The high places stay. When Baasha builds Ramah, Asa sends the temple’s silver and gold to Ben Hadad. Ben Hadad attacks Israel, and Asa builds Geba and Mizpah with Ramah’s stones.
asa.connections: Son of Abijam. Father of Jehoshaphat.

maacah-queen.name: Maacah
maacah-queen.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
maacah-queen.importance: She makes an image for an Asherah. Asa removes her from being queen. He cuts down her image and burns it at the brook Kidron.
maacah-queen.connections: Daughter of Abishalom. The text calls her mother of Abijam and of Asa.

ben-hadad-asa.name: Ben Hadad, Asa’s ally
ben-hadad-asa.role: King of Syria paid to attack Israel
ben-hadad-asa.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ben-hadad-asa.importance: Asa sends him silver and gold and asks him to break his treaty with Baasha. He agrees. His captains strike Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, and the land of Naphtali. Baasha then stops building Ramah.
ben-hadad-asa.connections: Son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion. The Ben Hadad who fights Ahab in chapter 20 appears to be a later king.

nadab.name: Nadab
nadab.role: King of Israel killed by Baasha
nadab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nadab.importance: He rules Israel two years and walks in his father’s way. Baasha kills him while Israel attacks Gibbethon. Baasha then kills all the house of Jeroboam.

baasha.name: Baasha
baasha.role: King of Israel who kills Nadab
baasha.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
baasha.importance: He kills Nadab at Gibbethon and wipes out Jeroboam’s house. He rules from Tirzah for twenty-four years and fights Asa. He builds Ramah but stops when Ben Hadad attacks. Jehu the son of Hanani tells him his own house will fall.
baasha.connections: Son of Ahijah of Issachar, who is not the prophet Ahijah. Father of Elah.

jehu-hanani.name: Jehu, Hanani’s son
jehu-hanani.role: Prophet who speaks against Baasha’s house
jehu-hanani.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehu-hanani.importance: He brings the LORD’s word against Baasha. Baasha walked in Jeroboam’s way, so his house will be swept away. Zimri later kills all the house of Baasha, as Jehu said.
jehu-hanani.connections: Son of Hanani. He is not Jehu the son of Nimshi.

elah.name: Elah
elah.role: King of Israel killed by his officer
elah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elah.importance: He rules Israel two years in Tirzah. He is drinking in Arza’s house when Zimri strikes him dead. Zimri then kills all the house of Baasha.
elah.connections: Son of Baasha. Zimri kills him at Tirzah.

zimri.name: Zimri
zimri.role: Chariot officer who rules for seven days
zimri.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zimri.importance: He kills Elah and all the house of Baasha. The army hears and makes Omri king. Omri takes Tirzah. Zimri burns the king’s house over himself and dies after seven days.
zimri.connections: Servant of Elah and captain of half his chariots. Omri’s army comes against him.

omri.name: Omri
omri.role: Army commander who becomes king and builds Samaria
omri.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
omri.importance: The army makes him king in the camp at Gibbethon. He takes Tirzah from Zimri and then beats Tibni’s side. He buys a hill from Shemer and builds Samaria. The text says he did more evil than all before him.
omri.connections: Opponent of Tibni. Father of Ahab.

tibni.name: Tibni
tibni.role: Rival of Omri for the throne
tibni.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
tibni.importance: Half the people follow Tibni to make him king. Half follow Omri. Omri’s side wins, Tibni dies, and Omri rules. The text does not say how Tibni dies.

shemer.name: Shemer
shemer.role: Owner of the hill of Samaria
shemer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shemer.importance: Omri buys the hill from him for two talents of silver. Omri builds a city there and names it Samaria after Shemer.
shemer.connections: He sells his hill to Omri.

ahab.name: Ahab
ahab.role: King of Israel faced by Elijah and Micaiah
ahab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahab.importance: He marries Jezebel and builds an altar for Baal in Samaria. He beats Ben Hadad twice but lets him go. He takes Naboth’s vineyard after Jezebel has Naboth killed. He ignores Micaiah’s warning and dies of an arrow wound at Ramoth Gilead.
ahab.connections: Son of Omri. Husband of Jezebel. Father of Ahaziah.

jezebel.name: Jezebel
jezebel.role: Queen who threatens Elijah and has Naboth killed
jezebel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jezebel.importance: She cuts off the LORD’s prophets. After Carmel she swears to kill Elijah. She writes letters in Ahab’s name so Naboth is accused and stoned. The LORD says dogs will eat her by Jezreel’s wall.
jezebel.connections: Daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Wife of Ahab.

hiel.name: Hiel
hiel.role: Man of Bethel who builds Jericho
hiel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hiel.importance: He builds Jericho in Ahab’s days. He lays its base at the loss of Abiram, his firstborn. He sets up its gates at the loss of Segub, his youngest. The text says this matches the LORD’s word by Joshua.

elijah.name: Elijah
elijah.role: Prophet who stands against Ahab and Baal
elijah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
locations: Cherith · broad eastern Jordan setting, exact brook unknown
Horeb · traditional Sinai region, identification disputed
elijah.importance: He tells Ahab no rain will fall, then hides at Cherith and Zarephath. On Mount Carmel he prays, fire falls, and he kills the prophets of Baal. He runs from Jezebel to Horeb, where the LORD gives him new work. He later tells Ahab his house will fall for Naboth’s death.
elijah.connections: A Tishbite from the settlers of Gilead. He calls Elisha to follow him.

zarephath-widow.name: The widow of Zarephath
zarephath-widow.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zarephath-widow.importance: She has one handful of meal and a little oil. She bakes for Elijah first, and the jars do not run out. When her son stops breathing, she blames Elijah. Elijah gives him back alive, and she calls Elijah a man of God.
zarephath-widow.connections: Mother of a son who falls sick and lives again.

zarephath-son.name: The widow’s son
zarephath-son.role: Unnamed boy whom Elijah’s prayer brings back
zarephath-son.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zarephath-son.importance: He falls sick until no breath is left in him. Elijah stretches over him three times and cries to the LORD. The child’s soul comes back, and Elijah gives him to his mother.
zarephath-son.connections: Son of the widow at Zarephath.

obadiah-palace.name: Obadiah
obadiah-palace.role: Palace official who hides the LORD’s prophets
obadiah-palace.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
obadiah-palace.importance: He hides one hundred prophets from Jezebel in caves and feeds them. Ahab sends him to look for grass, and he meets Elijah. He fears Ahab will kill him if Elijah is gone. He still goes and tells Ahab.
obadiah-palace.connections: He is over Ahab’s household and fears the LORD greatly.

elijah-servant.name: Elijah’s unnamed servant
elijah-servant.role: Helper who watches for the cloud
elijah-servant.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elijah-servant.importance: On Carmel, Elijah sends him seven times to look toward the sea. The seventh time he sees a small cloud like a man’s hand. Elijah sends him to warn Ahab of rain. Elijah later leaves his servant at Beersheba.
elijah-servant.connections: He serves Elijah. The text does not name him.

elisha.name: Elisha
elisha.role: Farmer whom Elijah calls with his mantle
elisha.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elisha.importance: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint him prophet in Elijah’s place. Elijah finds him plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and puts his mantle on him. Elisha kills his oxen, feeds the people, and follows Elijah. His later work is in 2 Kings.
elisha.connections: Son of Shaphat. From Abel Meholah.

hazael.name: Hazael
hazael.role: Man the LORD names as Syria’s next king
hazael.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hazael.importance: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint Hazael king over Syria. The LORD speaks of the sword of Hazael. Hazael does nothing in this book. His rise is told in 2 Kings.
hazael.connections: The LORD names him to Elijah at Horeb, with Jehu and Elisha.

jehu-nimshi.name: Jehu, Nimshi’s son
jehu-nimshi.role: Man the LORD names as Israel’s future king
jehu-nimshi.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehu-nimshi.importance: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint Jehu king over Israel. Jehu will kill those who escape Hazael’s sword. He does nothing in this book. 2 Kings tells how he takes power.
jehu-nimshi.connections: Son of Nimshi. He is not the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani.

ben-hadad-ahab.name: Ben Hadad, Ahab’s opponent
ben-hadad-ahab.role: King of Syria beaten and freed by Ahab
ben-hadad-ahab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ben-hadad-ahab.importance: He attacks Samaria and demands Ahab’s silver, gold, wives, and children. Israel beats him while he is drinking. The next year he loses again at Aphek and hides in an inner room. Ahab calls him brother, makes a covenant, and lets him go.
ben-hadad-ahab.connections: Thirty-two kings march with him. He appears to be a later king than Asa’s ally Ben Hadad.

ahab-prophets.name: The prophets who counsel Ahab
ahab-prophets.role: Unnamed prophets who speak to Ahab in chapter 20
ahab-prophets.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahab-prophets.importance: A prophet tells Ahab the LORD will give him the great army. A man of God promises a second win at Aphek. After Ahab frees Ben Hadad, one of the prophets waits for him in disguise. He tells Ahab his life will pay for the man he let go.
ahab-prophets.connections: They speak to Ahab during the wars with Ben Hadad. They are not the four hundred prophets of chapter 22.

naboth.name: Naboth
naboth.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
naboth.importance: Ahab offers to buy or trade for his vineyard. Naboth says he will not give up the land of his fathers. Jezebel has two men accuse him of cursing God and the king. He is stoned to death, and Ahab goes to take the vineyard.
naboth.connections: A man of Jezreel. His vineyard lies next to Ahab’s palace.

jehoshaphat.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat.role: King of Judah who asks for the LORD’s word
jehoshaphat.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoshaphat.importance: He agrees to go with Ahab to Ramoth Gilead. He asks for the LORD’s word first, and then for one more prophet. In battle the Syrians take him for Ahab until he cries out. He rules Judah twenty-five years and makes peace with Israel.
jehoshaphat.connections: Son of Asa and Azubah. Father of Jehoram.

micaiah.name: Micaiah
micaiah.role: Prophet who warns Ahab before battle
micaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
micaiah.importance: Told to agree with the other prophets, he first says, “Go up and prosper.” Ahab demands the truth. He tells of Israel scattered like sheep and of a lying spirit the LORD sent. Zedekiah strikes him, and Ahab sends him to prison.
micaiah.connections: Son of Imlah. Ahab hates him and puts him in prison.

zedekiah-chenaanah.name: Zedekiah
zedekiah-chenaanah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zedekiah-chenaanah.importance: He makes iron horns and says Ahab will push the Syrians with them. When Micaiah speaks of a lying spirit, he strikes Micaiah on the cheek. Micaiah says he will hide in an inner room.
zedekiah-chenaanah.connections: Son of Chenaanah. He is not the later king of Judah named Zedekiah.

amon-governor.name: Amon
amon-governor.role: City governor ordered to hold Micaiah
amon-governor.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
amon-governor.importance: Ahab orders Micaiah taken back to him. He is to keep Micaiah in prison on bread and water until Ahab returns. The text names him in one verse.
amon-governor.connections: He is named with Joash the king’s son. He is not the later king of Judah named Amon.

joash-prince.name: Joash
joash-prince.role: King’s son told to hold Micaiah
joash-prince.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joash-prince.importance: Ahab sends Micaiah back to him and to Amon. They are to keep Micaiah in prison until Ahab returns in peace. The text names him in one verse.
joash-prince.connections: Called the king’s son. He is named with Amon the governor.

ahaziah-ahab.name: Ahaziah
ahaziah-ahab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahaziah-ahab.importance: He becomes king in Samaria and rules two years. He asks to send his servants in Jehoshaphat’s ships, and Jehoshaphat refuses. He serves Baal as his father did. His story goes on in 2 Kings.

joab.name: Joab
joab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joab.importance: He helps Adonijah and eats at his feast. David tells Solomon that Joab killed Abner and Amasa in peace time. When Adonijah dies, Joab flees to the altar. Benaiah kills him there on Solomon’s order.
joab.connections: Son of Zeruiah. Brother of Abishai and Asahel.

nathan-prophet.name: Nathan
nathan-prophet.role: Prophet who helps Solomon become king
nathan-prophet.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nathan-prophet.importance: He tells Bathsheba that Adonijah is acting as king. He sends her to David and then comes in to back her words. David orders Solomon made king. Nathan and Zadok anoint Solomon at Gihon.
nathan-prophet.connections: He speaks to Bathsheba and to David. He works with Zadok and Benaiah.

hiram.name: Hiram
hiram.role: King of Tyre who sends Solomon wood and gold
hiram.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hiram.importance: He sends Solomon cedar and cypress wood, and Solomon pays in wheat and oil. Solomon gives him twenty cities in Galilee, and they do not please him. His sailors go with Solomon’s ships to Ophir for gold.
hiram.connections: He always loved David and makes a treaty with Solomon. He is not Hiram the bronze worker.

zadok.name: Zadok
zadok.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zadok.importance: He does not join Adonijah. At David’s order he takes the horn of oil from the Tent and anoints Solomon. Solomon then puts him in Abiathar’s place as priest.
zadok.connections: Son of Ahitub. Father of Ahimaaz.

benaiah.name: Benaiah
benaiah.role: Officer who carries out Solomon’s death orders
benaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
benaiah.importance: He does not join Adonijah and helps bring Solomon to Gihon. On Solomon’s orders he kills Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei. Solomon puts him over the army in Joab’s place.

bathsheba.name: Bathsheba
bathsheba.role: Solomon’s mother who speaks for him to David
bathsheba.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
bathsheba.importance: Nathan warns her, and she reminds David of his oath that Solomon will rule. David swears it again that day. Later Adonijah asks her to seek Abishag for him. She carries the request to Solomon, and Solomon has Adonijah killed.
bathsheba.connections: Daughter of Eliam. Wife of Uriah, later wife of David. Mother of Solomon.

shimei-gera.name: Shimei
shimei-gera.role: Benjamite told not to leave Jerusalem
shimei-gera.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shimei-gera.importance: David tells Solomon that Shimei once cursed him. Solomon orders Shimei to stay in Jerusalem or die. After three years Shimei goes to Gath to bring back two slaves. Solomon has Benaiah kill him.

jonathan-abiathar.name: Jonathan, Abiathar’s son
jonathan-abiathar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-abiathar.importance: He comes to Adonijah’s feast as the trumpet sounds. Adonijah expects good news. Jonathan says David has made Solomon king and Solomon sits on the throne. The guests are afraid and leave.
jonathan-abiathar.connections: Son of Abiathar the priest. He brings news to Adonijah.

amasa.name: Amasa
amasa.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
amasa.importance: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon that Joab killed him and Abner. Solomon gives this as a reason for Joab’s death.
amasa.connections: Son of Jether. His mother Abigail is the sister of Zeruiah.

barzillai.name: Barzillai
barzillai.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
barzillai.importance: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon to show kindness to his sons. They are to eat at Solomon’s table.
barzillai.connections: A Gileadite. His sons came to David when David fled from Absalom.

abner.name: Abner
abner.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abner.importance: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon that Joab killed him and Amasa. Solomon calls both men better than Joab.
abner.connections: Son of Ner. Captain of the army of Israel.

abiathar.name: Abiathar
abiathar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abiathar.importance: He helps Adonijah and eats at his feast. Solomon says he deserves death but spares him for his service to David. Solomon ends his work as priest and sends him to Anathoth. Chapter 4 still lists him as a priest.
abiathar.connections: Son of Ahimelech and father of Jonathan. He carried the ark before David.

david.name: David
david.role: Aging king who names Solomon as successor
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: He is old and cold when Adonijah claims the throne. Bathsheba and Nathan remind him of his oath, and he has Solomon anointed. He tells Solomon to keep God’s law and to deal with Joab and Shimei. After his death the LORD spares part of the kingdom for his sake.
david.connections: Son of Jesse. Father of Amnon, Absalom, Tamar, Solomon, and other children.
